newsitem.title: UK: S&P cuts Sainsbury's, unit ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts Sainsbury's, unit ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poors said on Thursday it had downgraded its long-term rating on J.Sainsbury plc and its guaranteed related entity to A plus from AA minus, and short-term to A1 from A1 plus.
The outlook has been revised to stable from negative, S&P said in a statement.

"This rating action reflects a perceived weakening of the group's business and financial profiles, largely a result of the very competitive and capital intensive nature of the British grocery retailing sector, and the group's small but increased exposure to the challenging DIY market in the Britain," S&P said.
"Sainsbury's leading market position in British grocery retailing continues to underpin the group's strong credit profile even in a highly competitive industry environment," the agency said.
"Current high levels of capital expenditure are constraining the group's generation of discretionary cash flow, but are expected to increase future returns on investment," S&P said.
S&P said The British grocery retailing sector, where Sainsbury's is a leading player, still accounted for the vast majority of group sales, profits and net assets.
"The heightened pace of competition in recent years, combined with little or no growth in British consumer spending, has reduced the attractiveness of the sector as a whole," it said.

"Also, Sainsbury's traditional leadership position in British grocery retailing has been challenged by other competitors which has resulted in modest margin slippage in fiscal 1996 which may be difficult to recover in such a competitive environment," S&P said.

"In recent years Sainsbury's has started to invest in other highly competitive but related areas such as British do-it-yourself (DIY) through its Homebase and Texas formats and in U.S. food retailing through Shaw's and a 20 percent stake in Giant Food Inc.," it said.

"Sainsbury continues to maintain its industry-leading profitability among British supermarket retailers. Through a combination of high market share, an attractive own-label portfolio and cost-cutting measures, the group maintains a strong British position," S&P said.
"However, sustained pricing pressure in Britain combined with increased emphasis on marketing activities is negatively impacting margins," it said.
S&P said the following ratings had been downgraded.
RATINGS LOWERED TO FROM
J.Sainsbury Plc
Senior unsecured A plus AA minus
Subordinated A A plus
Commercial paper A1 A1 plus
J.Sainsbury (Channel Islands) Ltd. (Subordinated Guarantor: J.Sainsbury Plc)
Subordinated A A plus
--International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 4041
